text:
{
  "status": "NEEDS_IMPROVEMENT",
  "SYSTEM_INTERPRETATION_OF_USER_INTENT": "The system interprets past purchases and listening as continued demand for broadly related items, with limited attention to the specific purpose or occasion behind them.",
  "WHERE_THE_SYSTEM_GETS_IT_RIGHT": [
    "Recommendations align when they extend a specific recurring interest, such as a familiar artist, compatible replacement supply, or established circuit-building activity.",
    "Related items appeal when they preserve the qualities users value or add a useful capability to equipment they already own."
  ],
  "WHERE_THE_SYSTEM_GETS_IT_WRONG": [
    "Broadly related products compete with stronger matches despite serving different tasks, requiring unsupported equipment, or lacking a clear connection to repeated interests.",
    "Recent ownership is treated as demand for similar devices or supplies even when the purchase has already satisfied the need.",
    "Seasonal and isolated interactions are extended into ongoing preferences without sufficient support from the surrounding history."
  ],
  "OVERUSED_DECISION_PATTERNS": [
    "Broad category, ecosystem, genre, and collection-format similarity substitutes for specific functional or content relevance.",
    "A single related purchase is generalized into demand for replacements, additional devices, or supplies for unrelated projects."
  ],
  "UNDERUSED_OR_MISSED_DECISION_PATTERNS": [
    "Repeated, recent interests receive insufficient priority over isolated or older interactions.",
    "Compatibility, dimensions, connectors, and task requirements are insufficiently reflected in practical-product matches.",
    "Rankings insufficiently distinguish useful additions from redundant purchases and occasion-dependent interests from persistent preferences.",
    "Specific artists, musical qualities, and story characteristics provide stronger choice signals than broad entertainment categories."
  ],
  "PRIMARY_FAILURE_MODE_AT_TOP_OF_LIST": "Top-ranked items often share a broad association with history but lack the specific relevance, compatibility, or unmet purpose needed to motivate a choice now.",
  "DIAGNOSTIC_SIGNALS_TO_TRACK": [
    "The proportion of top-ranked recommendations users identify as choices they would make now, separated from merely plausible matches.",
    "The frequency of top-ranked rejections attributed to redundancy, incompatible specifications, unsupported projects, or occasion mismatch.",
    "The ranking of items supported by repeated recent interests relative to items supported only by broad similarity or isolated interactions.",
    "The rate of relevance judgments that remain indeterminate because available item content is insufficient, tracked separately from explicit mismatches."
  ]
}
